questions.text:
Suppose we are given [latex]n[/latex] keys, [latex]m[/latex] hash table slots, and two simple uniform hash functions [latex]h_1[/latex] and [latex]h_2[/latex]. Further suppose our hashing scheme uses [latex]h_1[/latex] for the odd keys
and [latex]h_2[/latex] for the even keys. What is the expected number of keys in a slot?
questions.solution:
Both [latex]h_1[/latex] and [latex]h_2[/latex] are simple uniform hash functions, so every key (odd or even) lands in any given slot with probability [latex]\frac{1}{m}[/latex].

Expected keys in a slot [latex]=n\times\frac{1}{m}=\frac{n}{m}[/latex] (which hash function is used does not matter).

Answer: [latex]\frac{n}{m}[/latex]

questions.text: Which one of the following facilitates transfer of bulk data from hard disk to main memory with the highest throughput?
questions.solution:
In DMA, the DMA controller moves the whole block between disk and memory directly, without the CPU handling every word. Interrupt-driven, polling and programmed I/O all need the CPU for each word, so they are much slower for bulk data.

Answer: DMA based I/O transfer

questions.text: Let R1 and R2 be two 4-bit registers that store numbers in 2's complement form. For the operation R1+R2, which one of the following values of R1 and R2 gives an arithmetic overflow?
questions.solution:
4-bit 2's complement range: [latex]-8[/latex] to [latex]+7[/latex].

- 1011 + 1110 = [latex](-5)+(-2)=-7[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits
- 1100 + 1010 = [latex](-4)+(-6)=-10[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] overflow
- 0011 + 0100 = [latex]3+4=7[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits
- 1001 + 1111 = [latex](-7)+(-1)=-8[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits

Answer: R1 = 1100 and R2 = 1010

questions.text:
Consider the following threads, [latex]T_1, T_2, \text{ and }T_3[/latex] executing on a single processor, synchronized using three binary semaphore variables, [latex]S_1, S_2, \text{ and }S_3[/latex], operated upon using standard [latex]wait()[/latex] and [latex]signal()[/latex]. The threads can be context switched in any order and at any time.

Which initialization of the semaphores would print the sequence BCABCABCA ...?
questions.solution:
From the code: T2 prints B (needs [latex]S_1[/latex], then signals [latex]S_3[/latex]), T1 prints C (needs [latex]S_3[/latex], signals [latex]S_2[/latex]), T3 prints A (needs [latex]S_2[/latex], signals [latex]S_1[/latex]).

The output must start with B, so only T2 may run first: [latex]S_1=1[/latex] and [latex]S_2=S_3=0[/latex]. Then the chain B [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B [latex]\ldots[/latex] repeats forever.

(If [latex]S_2[/latex] or [latex]S_3[/latex] were 1, A or C could be printed first.)

Answer: [latex]S_1=1;\ S_2=0;\ S_3=0[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following two statements with respect to the matrices [latex]A_{m \times n},B_{n \times m},C_{n \times n} \text{ and }D_{n \times n},[/latex]

Statement 1: [latex]tr(AB) = tr(BA)[/latex]
Statement 2: [latex]tr(CD) = tr(DC)[/latex]

where[latex]tr()[/latex] represents the trace of a matrix. Which one of the following holds?
questions.solution:
[latex]tr(AB)=\sum_i\sum_k a_{ik}b_{ki}=\sum_k\sum_i b_{ki}a_{ik}=tr(BA)[/latex]. This holds for any [latex]A_{m\times n}[/latex], [latex]B_{n\times m}[/latex] (AB is [latex]m\times m[/latex], BA is [latex]n\times n[/latex]).

Statement 2 is the special case of square matrices, so it is also true.

Answer: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
